name: HumanoidBench
ability_definition: The ability to coordinate the movement of your arms, legs, and torso together when the whole body is in motion.

task_realism.reasoning: The 31 tasks map onto recognizable whole-body activities that appear in physical work: walking, running, climbing stairs, crawling, hurdling, balancing, sliding, and loco-manipulation such as carrying or pushing objects. Success requires coordinating the legs, torso and arms together. However, the tasks are stylized, reward-shaped scenarios in clean simulated scenes, not actual job tasks like moving freight on a loading dock or navigating a cluttered construction site.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation happens entirely in simulation (MuJoCo, Unitree H1 model). Agents often have privileged or low-noise state and no sim-to-real gap. They are trained per task over millions of steps, and budgets and protocols vary across papers. There are no real physical stakes, fatigue, unmodeled contact dynamics, or unstructured environmental variation. Workplace gross body coordination has to generalize immediately under noisy, novel conditions, which this setup does not test.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Coverage of the dynamic whole-body movement space is broad: locomotion across varied terrain plus whole-body manipulation with dexterous hands, all on a 61-actuator humanoid. Several things are missing: robustness to perturbations in the wild, transfer across tasks with a single policy, sustained or prolonged activity, and coordination in cooperative settings with people. Results are also per-task specialists rather than one general coordinating agent.

format_match.reasoning: Actions are joint-level control commands, which is structurally analogous to motor output. Inputs, however, are simulator state vectors, and outcomes are scalar episode returns against author-set thresholds rather than completed work artifacts. The lack of a canonical aggregate metric further separates the output format from real-world performance judgments.

transferability_reasoning: HumanoidBench genuinely requires coordinated arm, leg and torso control across diverse dynamic tasks, so it targets the right construct better than most benchmarks. Its transfer to real workplace gross body coordination is limited by purely simulated, per-task-trained evaluation without real-world noise, stakes, or physical embodiment. Scores reflect learned simulated control policies rather than demonstrated physical capability.

2024.metric: per-task maximum episode return (task-specific scale, each task has its own success target)

2026.metric: mean success-normalized score across the 14 h1hand tasks, as a percentage: (return - random) / (task success threshold - random) x 100. The paper reports 0.534, 95% CI [0.473, 0.595].
2026.human_reference: General adult workforce performing whole-body physical work (e.g., laborers, warehouse staff, construction workers) whose jobs require walking, running, crawling, climbing stairs, hurdling, balancing and whole-body manipulation.
